question: Where can I get electricity consumption by municipality or postal code in the United States, by sector and year?

answer.summary: No national dataset: EIA-861 gives sales (MWh) by utility, state and sector, and only lists counties served. Local metered data exist state by state: New York's Utility Energy Registry gives monthly MWh by city/town/village and sector (ZIP only for NYC) via open API; PG&E publishes monthly kWh by ZIP and customer type (download behind a form); some utilities send cities annual reports (e.g. Xcel). ZIP codes are not Census ZCTAs.
main_caveats: No federal source gives municipal or ZIP consumption; EIA-861 is by utility and state, and its county list is service territory without sales.
Local data are privacy-screened: withheld sectors (NY -999), merged ZIPs (PG&E) or merged classes (Xcel).
USPS ZIP codes used by utilities are delivery-based and differ from Census ZCTAs and from municipal boundaries.
Utility totals cover only that utility's customers; municipalities served by several utilities need all of them.
answer.confidence_reason: NY registry fully tested via API and EIA checked; California tested only at page level (form), other states sampled with one Xcel report.

sources.publisher: New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA), data reported by utilities under NY PSC Case 17-M-0315

unit.value: MWh for consumption fields (unit column; both 'MWh' and 'MWH' spellings occur).

inclusion_rule.value: Utilities and CCA administrators under PSC regulation must report community energy use.
inclusion_rule.quote: The order requires utilities and CCA administrators under its regulation to develop and report community energy use data to the UER.

reference_date.value: Calendar year and month per row; latest month 2026-06 in the community and ZIP datasets on 2026-11-26.

exclusions.value: Sector values withheld (-999) when fewer than 4 accounts; ZIP data only for New York City.
exclusions.quote: If there are fewer than 4 accounts in a given sector within a ZIP code the entire sector for that ZIP code is withheld.     ZIP code level-data are only reported for ZIP codes located in New York City.

key_fields.meaning: Calendar period of the consumption (not publication date)
Municipality (City, Town, Village, Borough, Reservation) with Census place FIPS
USPS ZIP code (ZIP dataset g2x3-izm4); multiple rows when served by more than one utility
Consumption in MWh; -999 withheld for privacy; blank not reported

how_to_use.example_request: https://data.ny.gov/resource/4txm-py4p.json?$select=month,uer_id,value,number_of_accounts&$where=com_name='Albany' AND com_type='City' AND data_field='3_nat_consumption' AND year=2025&$order=month
steps: Community dataset 4txm-py4p (3,990,470 rows, 2021-2026); ZIP dataset g2x3-izm4 (371,759 rows, NYC ZIPs); county dataset 46pe-aat9; 2016-2020 archives m3xm-q3dw, tzb9-c2c6, 47km-hhvs under a previous protocol.
Filter data_class='electricity' and data_field in 1/8/9/2/3_nat_consumption; sum value by year after checking which months are present.
Add rows from all utilities (uer_id) serving the municipality; treat -999 as withheld, not zero.
reading_traps: Months are missing by utility and half-year: Albany City total consumption has months 7-12 in 2021, 1-6 in 2023 and 2025, all 12 in 2024; statewide row counts per month drop from 1,044 to 87 in early 2021 and to 580 in late 2023.
The 2016-2021 archive was collected under a previous data protocol and its community dataset ends in 2020 despite the title; series are not directly comparable across the 2021 break.
ZIP-code data exist only for New York City ZIP codes; outside NYC use municipality or county.
Residential consumption was withheld (-999) in 176 of 15,788 municipality-month rows in 2025.
Utilities alone are responsible for the data; NYSERDA does not warrant accuracy (dataset disclaimer).

evidence.quote: On April 19, 2018, the New York State Public Service Commission (PSC) issued the Order Adopting the Utility Energy Registry under regulatory CASE 17-M-0315.
It is important to note that the data are subject to privacy screening and fields that fail the privacy screen are withheld.

unit.quote: Customer usage data, both for gas (therms) and electric (kWh) usage, is reported by ZIP code, by month, by year, and by the four customer types – residential, commercial, agricultural and industrial.

inclusion_rule.value: Aggregation thresholds of CPUC D.14-05-016: 100 residential / 15 non-residential customers, no customer above 15%.
inclusion_rule.quote: a minimum of 100 Residential customers; a minimum of 15 Non-Residential customers, with no single Non-Residential customer accounting for more than 15% of the total consumption.

reference_date.value: Each file holds 3 months through the quarter in its name; latest listed PGE_2026_Q3.
reference_date.quote: contain 3 months of usage data that is through the end of the calendar quarter indicated in the file name.

update_frequency.quote: Subsequent reports will be published quarterly, 15 days after the end of each quarter.

exclusions.value: ZIP codes below the threshold are merged with a neighbouring ZIP; net-metered customers reported at net values.
exclusions.quote: If aggregation is not met, the consumption will be combined with a neighboring ZIP code until the aggregation requirements are met.

key_fields.meaning: USPS ZIP code (possibly combined with a neighbour)

how_to_use.example_result: HTTP 200 text/html: form 'Please enter the following details before downloading data.' with organization_name, name, email and agreement checkboxes (file not downloaded).
steps: List of quarterly files from PGE_2013_Q1 to PGE_2026_Q3 on the public data sets page.
Download requires submitting organization, name, email and accepting the D.14-05-016 terms.
reading_traps: The page says the first reports were PGE_2014_Q3 covering October 2013-September 2014, yet the list shows files labelled 2013 Q1-Q4; the difference was not resolved.
Merged ZIP codes mean a row can represent several ZIPs.
Net-metered customers are included at net monthly values, which understates gross consumption.
